import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A Brightwater maintenance ticket needs a place for the warehouse to discuss
the repair and to keep the photos of the damage. Facet puts both beside the
document: a **comments** panel and an **attachments** panel. The records live
in their own doctypes in the `core` domain — the engine calls this shape a
**sidecar**, and that is the last time this page uses the word. The host
doctype declares which panels it carries; one declaration serves every
doctype that wants the panel, so you never copy the comment logic into your
domain.

## When to use this

Add the `comments` panel when people discuss a record. Add the `attachments`
panel when people keep files with a record. Both panels are declared on the
doctype, so you can give them to any doctype in your domain.

## Before you start

- **A draft domain.** You edit the host doctype in a [draft domain](/build/model/in-app/how-drafts-work/), or in the
  [domain folder on a dev server](/build/model/in-files/domain-files/).
- **Nothing to create.** The panel doctypes `core.Comment` and
  `core.Attachment` exist on every instance. You declare them on your host;
  you do not create them.
- **A free segment name.** A segment name (the panel's route segment, such as
  `comments`) cannot collide with a `children` relationship of the same name.

## Steps

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the doctype in the **Builder** and find the **Sidecars** section.
2. Add an entry per panel: the segment name (`comments`, `attachments`) and
   the panel doctype (`core.Comment`, `core.Attachment`).
3. Optionally set a **Label** (for example `Notes`) and an **Order** for the
   tab.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Files">

The Brightwater ticket carries both panels, exactly as the bundle ships it:

```yaml
# equipment/doctypes/equipment.MaintenanceTicket.yml (extract)
sidecars:
  comments:
    doctype: core.Comment
    column: target
  attachments:
    doctype: core.Attachment
    column: target
```

The `column` names the reference field on the panel doctype that points back
at the host. `target` is the default and almost always right.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Check the rights

A nested panel grant follows the host path. In practice:

| Caller right | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| read on `equipment.MaintenanceTicket` | Read the comments and attachments. |
| create on `equipment.MaintenanceTicket` | Write comments and attach files. |
| create on `equipment.MaintenanceTicket.Comment` | Comment as a read-only user. |

That last line is how you let a viewer comment: keep their host rights
read-only and add the explicit nested line for the action.

### See the panel

Open a document. The panel stands beside the page and shows one tab per
declared panel, with a count per tab. Comments take markdown, support
replies, and notify a person when you mention them. Attachments show type,
size, uploader, and time.

A mention is a link to an account. Both forms work in a comment body:

```markdown
Ping [Tom](urn:facet:iam:Account:tom@brightwater.example) about the pole set.
```

## Example

The panel API creates a comment through the host path:

```sh
curl -k -X POST "https://facet.localhost:3443/Api/equipment/MaintenanceTicket/MT-2026-0001/comments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FACET_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"body": "Pole set frayed at the joint — photos attached."}'
```

`-k` skips the certificate check of the local development address. Facet sets
the `target` from the path and the `author` from the caller. A `target` key
in the body answers `400` — the route owns that field.

## Troubleshooting

### The panel does not show

The doctype carries no `sidecars` map, or the doctype was edited after the
page was opened. Check the definition and reload.

### Commenting answers `403`

Your role can read the host but holds no create right on the host path and no
explicit nested line. Ask the domain author for `create` on the host, or for
the nested line shown in the rights table.

### A flat create of `core.Comment` answers `422`

Panel records are created through the host document, never through the flat
route. Use the nested path shown in the example.

### The comments are gone after a delete

Deleting the host removes its panel records through an event-driven sweep. If
the host document itself is rolled back, the sweep's removals stay — the
comments do not come back with the host.
